chunks: Al-Sharif Abu Ya'la al-Ja'fari (may God have mercy on him) — the successor of the described Sheikh, his student who sat in his place after him, and his son-in-law — said:
The Sheikh would not sleep at night except for a brief doze, then he would rise to pray, or to read and study, or to teach, or to recite the Quran.

key_terms.الْمُتَرْجَمِ لَهُ: the one whose biography is being written — i.e. Sheikh al-Mufid; a technical term of Islamic biographical literature
key_terms.الْهَجْعَةَ: a brief doze or light slumber; the minimal sleep the Sheikh permitted himself at night
key_terms.صِهْرَهُ: his son-in-law, indicating the close familial and scholarly bond between Abu Ya'la and the Sheikh

ai.seo_question: What was Sheikh al-Mufid's nightly routine according to his student and successor al-Sharif Abu Ya'la al-Ja'fari?
ai.summary: Al-Sharif Abu Ya'la al-Ja'fari — successor, student, and son-in-law of Sheikh al-Mufid — testifies that the Sheikh slept at night only the briefest of dozes, then rose to pray, read, teach, or recite the Quran. This biographical attestation highlights the ascetic piety and tireless scholarly and devotional activity of Sheikh al-Mufid.
